title: WhatsApp pricing changes on October 1, 2026
summary: On October 1, 2026 WhatsApp starts charging for support replies and in-window utility templates. What changes, what it costs, and what to check first.
body_markdown:
**On October 1, 2026, two things become billable on the WhatsApp Business Platform.** Free-form replies inside the 24-hour customer service window are charged as service messages, having been free since November 2024. Utility templates sent in response to a customer are charged inside that same window, having been free since July 2025.


If most of your WhatsApp volume is promotional campaigns, very little changes. If it is support conversations and order updates, you get a new line on the invoice where there used to be a zero.


What you send Before Oct 1, 2026 From Oct 1, 2026


Free-form reply inside the 24-hour window Free since Nov 2024 Charged at the market's utility rate


Utility template inside the 24-hour window Free since Jul 2025 Charged at the market's utility rate


Marketing templates Charged Charged, same rates


Inbound messages and customer-initiated calls Free Free


Anything inside the 72-hour free entry point window Free Free


To put your own numbers against both rate cards, use the[WhatsApp pricing calculator](https://www.courier.com/tools/whatsapp-pricing-calculator) . For the full pricing model rather than this one change, see the[guide to WhatsApp Business Platform pricing](https://www.courier.com/guides/whatsapp-pricing) .


## What changes on October 1, 2026


Two changes, both documented by Meta on its[pricing for non-template messages](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/non-template-messages) page.


**Service messages become billable.** A service message is any free-form message you send inside an open customer service window: a plain text reply, an image, a document, a set of reply buttons. These have been free since November 2024. From October 1 they are charged per message, at the same rate your market pays for utility and authentication messages. There are no volume discounts on them.


**Utility templates in the window become billable.** Since July 2025, a utility template delivered while the customer service window was open cost nothing. That concession ends. The same template is charged whether the window is open or shut.


## What is not changing


Four things this change does not touch, since it is often described more broadly than it is.


- **Marketing template rates.** Unaffected by this change.
- **Inbound messages.** Anything a customer sends you is still free, as are calls they start.
- **The 24-hour window itself.** It still opens and resets on every customer message or call. What you are permitted to send is unchanged. Only the price changes.
- **The 72-hour free entry point window.** Reply to someone who arrived from a Click to WhatsApp ad and the next 72 hours of messages remain free.
- **Volume discounts on utility and authentication.** Still six bands per market, down to 25% off, or 30% in India.


## How much more will you pay?


Take a shop sending to customers in Brazil, where utility, authentication and service messages each cost $0.0068 and marketing costs $0.0625. Its traffic does not change at all, only what Meta charges for it:


What it sends each month Before Oct 1, 2026 From Oct 1, 2026


20,000 promotions $1,250.00 $1,250.00


30,000 login codes $204.00 $204.00


10,000 order updates sent inside the window $0 $68.00


20,000 support replies $0 $136.00


**Monthly total** **$1,454.00** **$1,658.00**


A 14% rise on a bill that was not otherwise going to move, and all of it lands on the two bottom lines.


Country matters more than volume here. The same two new lines cost $1,650 a month if those customers are in Germany rather than Brazil, because a message there is $0.0550 instead of $0.0068. Put your own markets in the[pricing calculator](https://www.courier.com/tools/whatsapp-pricing-calculator) rather than scaling one country's number.


## Why is Meta charging for service messages?


The change arrives alongside the Meta Business Agent Platform, which launched on July 1, 2026 and became billable on August 1, 2026. Meta charges for agent replies per token, at $2.00 per million tokens worldwide, which works out to roughly 4 to 5 cents for a typical reply.


Once Meta sells an AI agent that answers customers inside the conversation window, free unlimited replies in that same window stop making commercial sense. October 1 closes the gap between what Meta's own agent costs and what a human or third-party agent costs.


## What to do before October 1, 2026


**Measure your service message volume.** Query the Pricing Analytics API for a` pricing_category` of` SERVICE` over a full month. That count, multiplied by your market's utility rate, is the new line on your invoice. Most teams have never had a reason to look at this number, and the[pricing calculator](https://www.courier.com/tools/whatsapp-pricing-calculator) will total it across markets once you have it.


**Count your in-window utility templates.** Before October 1, 2026 their status webhooks carry` type: free_customer_service` with` category: utility` . From October 1 the same messages carry` type: regular` . Every one of those becomes a charge.


**Look at thread length.** A ten-message support exchange was free. From October 1, 2026 it is ten charges. Deflection, better first answers, and shorter threads become a cost lever rather than a service metric.


**Check your template categories while you are in there.** This is unrelated to October 1, but it is the most common source of surprise WhatsApp costs. A single promotional sentence in an order update recategorises the whole template as marketing. In Germany that moves a message from $0.0550 to $0.1365. The[guide covers how Meta assigns and silently changes categories](https://www.courier.com/guides/whatsapp-pricing) .


**Review which notifications belong on WhatsApp at all.** While replies were free, WhatsApp was the cheapest place to hold a conversation. October 1, 2026 changes that calculation, and some of what you send over WhatsApp may be better served by email, SMS or in-app.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is changing in WhatsApp pricing on October 1, 2026?


Two things become billable. Free-form replies sent inside the 24-hour customer service window, which have been free since November 2024, and utility templates sent in response to a customer inside that window, which have been free since July 2025. Both are charged at the same rate your market pays for utility and authentication messages.


### How much do WhatsApp service messages cost?


The same as utility and authentication messages in that market, which is $0.0068 in Brazil, $0.0034 in the United States and Canada, $0.0014 in India and $0.0550 in Germany. Unlike utility and authentication, service messages get no volume discounts, so the rate does not fall as you send more.


### Are WhatsApp marketing message rates changing on October 1, 2026?


No. This change affects service messages and in-window utility templates only. Separately, nine markets move out of regional pricing onto their own rate card lines on the same date, which changes rates for Bangladesh, Iraq, Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Morocco, Nepal, Oman, Sri Lanka and Ukraine.


### Will my WhatsApp bill go up?


If your volume is mostly promotional campaigns, barely. If it is support conversations and order updates, you get a line on the bill that was not there before. In the example above, a Brazilian shop's bill rises 14% on identical traffic. The same traffic in a more expensive market rises far more.


### Is the 24-hour customer service window going away?


No. It still opens when a customer messages or calls you and resets on each new message from them, and it still governs whether you can send free-form messages at all. Only the price of messages sent inside it changes.


### When exactly does the WhatsApp price change take effect?


On October 1, 2026, at midnight in each WhatsApp Business Account's own timezone. Meta only changes pricing on the first day of a quarter, and commits to one month's notice for rate changes and six months for a change of pricing model.


### Do I need to do anything before October 1, 2026?


Nothing is required to keep sending, and no migration or setting change is involved. What is worth doing is measuring: count your service messages and your in-window utility templates for a full month, so the new invoice line is a number you already expected rather than a surprise.


### How do I find out how many service messages I send?


Query the Pricing Analytics API with a` pricing_category` of` SERVICE` for a full month. You can also check message status webhooks for a` pricing` object with` type` set to` free_customer_service` , which is what these messages carry before October 1, 2026.
